{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts",
      "line": 144,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "One-time backup code can be replayed in concurrent login attempts",
      "body": "The backup code verification and invalidation are not atomic. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check (line 144) before either updates the database (line 149). Both would then set the same index to null and update the user record, effectively allowing the same one-time code to authenticate multiple sessions. An attacker who obtains a valid backup code (e.g., via shoulder surfing) could exploit this race to gain multiple valid sessions."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 135,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "`onEnable` callback is not fired immediately after enabling 2FA",
      "body": "In `handleEnable`, after a successful enable API call (response.status === 200), the code only sets the step to `DisplayBackupCodes` and does not call `onEnable`. Previously, `onEnable` was invoked immediately to notify the parent that 2FA was enabled. Now `onEnable` is only called when the user clicks the 'close' button on the backup codes screen. If the user dismisses the dialog by clicking outside, pressing Escape, or using any other close mechanism (which triggers `onOpenChange`), `onEnable` is never called, leaving the parent component (e.g., the settings page) in a stale state where 2FA appears disabled until a refresh."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx",
      "line": 98,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Object URL from Blob is not revoked on modal reset or unmount",
      "body": "In `handleSetup`, a Blob URL is created with `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. While the code revokes the previous URL before creating a new one, it never revokes the URL when the component is unmounted or when `resetState` is called (e.g., on cancel or close). This causes a memory leak of the object URL, especially if a user repeatedly starts and cancels the 2FA setup flow."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx",
      "line": 7,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "style",
      "title": "Component is named `TwoFactor` instead of `BackupCode`",
      "body": "The default export function is named `TwoFactor`, but the file and its purpose are for entering a backup code. This is likely a copy-paste error that will cause confusion during imports and debugging, and it violates the principle of least surprise for maintainers."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts",
      "line": 12,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "No tests for backup code login or disabling 2FA with backup code",
      "body": "The PR introduces backup code functionality for both login and disabling 2FA, but the only added tests cover displaying, downloading, and copying the codes during setup. There are no tests that verify a backup code can be used to log in, that it is invalidated after use, or that it can be used to disable 2FA. Given the security-sensitive nature of one-time backup codes, missing tests for the core flows increase the risk of regressions."
    }

findings.title: One-time backup code can be replayed in concurrent login attempts
findings.body: The backup code verification and invalidation are not atomic. Two concurrent login requests using the same backup code can both pass the `indexOf` check (line 144) before either updates the database (line 149). Both would then set the same index to null and update the user record, effectively allowing the same one-time code to authenticate multiple sessions. An attacker who obtains a valid backup code (e.g., via shoulder surfing) could exploit this race to gain multiple valid sessions.

findings.title: `onEnable` callback is not fired immediately after enabling 2FA
findings.body: In `handleEnable`, after a successful enable API call (response.status === 200), the code only sets the step to `DisplayBackupCodes` and does not call `onEnable`. Previously, `onEnable` was invoked immediately to notify the parent that 2FA was enabled. Now `onEnable` is only called when the user clicks the 'close' button on the backup codes screen. If the user dismisses the dialog by clicking outside, pressing Escape, or using any other close mechanism (which triggers `onOpenChange`), `onEnable` is never called, leaving the parent component (e.g., the settings page) in a stale state where 2FA appears disabled until a refresh.

findings.title: Object URL from Blob is not revoked on modal reset or unmount
findings.body: In `handleSetup`, a Blob URL is created with `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. While the code revokes the previous URL before creating a new one, it never revokes the URL when the component is unmounted or when `resetState` is called (e.g., on cancel or close). This causes a memory leak of the object URL, especially if a user repeatedly starts and cancels the 2FA setup flow.

findings.title: Component is named `TwoFactor` instead of `BackupCode`
findings.body: The default export function is named `TwoFactor`, but the file and its purpose are for entering a backup code. This is likely a copy-paste error that will cause confusion during imports and debugging, and it violates the principle of least surprise for maintainers.

findings.title: No tests for backup code login or disabling 2FA with backup code
findings.body: The PR introduces backup code functionality for both login and disabling 2FA, but the only added tests cover displaying, downloading, and copying the codes during setup. There are no tests that verify a backup code can be used to log in, that it is invalidated after use, or that it can be used to disable 2FA. Given the security-sensitive nature of one-time backup codes, missing tests for the core flows increase the risk of regressions.
